summary: Earth Trend Detective helps people explore how environmental conditions change over time. Users choose a location on an interactive map, select variables such as temperature, rainfall, or humidity, and request historical data from NASA POWER. The app turns daily or monthly records into annual values, displays the time series, and estimates the trend using linear regression, the Mann–Kendall test, and Sen’s slope. Optional NASA FIRMS fire detections add recent fire hotspots to the map, while NASA CMR helps find records for OPERA Sentinel-1 radar scenes. The project makes Earth data easier for students and the public to explore, while explaining that a statistical trend shows a pattern and does not, by itself, prove its cause.
details: Earth Trend Detective is an interactive web app built with Python and Streamlit. It uses the NASA POWER Manager API to find available environmental variables and the NASA POWER Daily or Monthly Point API to retrieve historical values for a selected location. The app aggregates records into annual values, charts the series, and estimates trends using ordinary least squares, the Mann–Kendall test, and Sen’s slope. Users select locations from markers on a map with CARTO basemap tiles. Optional features use the NASA FIRMS Area API to display recent VIIRS fire detections and NASA’s Common Metadata Repository (CMR) Search API to find OPERA RTC-S1 Sentinel-1 radar scene records. The current CMR feature searches scene information; it does not download or analyze radar image pixels. The app is intended as an educational exploration tool. Trends are exploratory and do not establish what caused the change. Tools used include Python, Streamlit, Plotly, and ChatGPT assistance for code and writing.
